Data notes for this edition
  • A clean scan. The collector finished at 07:43 ET Friday and every symbol ends on Thursday Nov 5's completed bar on every frame; no pre-market stub was found and nothing was patched. The weekly column is the running Nov 2–6 bar, four sessions old, and its badges are provisional until today's close.
  • Deltas are one session. The prior scan is Thursday morning's, which held Wednesday Nov 4's close, so the change chips, the breadth tile and the census all measure Thursday's session.
  • Weekday names. "Thursday" in a card is Nov 5, "Wednesday" Nov 4, "Tuesday" Nov 3, "Monday" Nov 2 and "Friday" Oct 30; today's session is "today" or "the open". Hours are named by the time they open: "the first hour" is 09:30–10:30, "the 10:30 hour" the second, "the last hour" 15:30–16:00. Every time in this report is Eastern standard time.
  • The weekly column is provisional and today's close decides it. SPY's running close sits 19.57 under its 752.57 weekly EMA21 after 30 completed weeks over it; QQQ sits 56.62 under its own, SMH 99.63 under, NVDA 29.34 under, MSFT 47.44 over. Five weekly badges moved on Thursday's bar: SPY, IGV, AMZN and PLTR came off up to mixed and TSLA turned down from mixed. Only today's close counts.
  • The prints. IONQ reported Thursday after the close; its direction is not on the feed and its card opens on gap rules. AMD is two sessions past its print and its card trades Thursday's bar. CRWV reports Tue Nov 10 and NVDA Tue Nov 17, both after the close; CRWV carries the event tag, NVDA is seven sessions out.
  • The feed. Direction only: the worst selloff since the 2025 tariff shock, AI stocks hit on the midterm result, a Democratic sweep and the rate path, Asian chip stocks lower, Nasdaq futures higher before the open. No price or percentage from a headline appears in this report, and no card's level comes from the pre-market.
  • Volume. The median print was 2.06× the 20-day average against Wednesday's 1.39×, and every one of the 25 names printed over its average; SNDK 3.38×, XLK 3.29×, SPY 3.08×, QQQ 3.03×, AMD 3.02× and NVDA 2.96× led, META 1.18×, CRWV 1.33× and ORCL 1.36× were the lightest. 15-minute volume figures are not used.
  • Eight cards carry a daily chart: MSFT, AAPL, AMZN, NVDA, AMD, TSLA, MU and SNDK. Six stances changed on their cards' own rules, three of them upgrades printed on the day the index fell 4.4%: MSFT and AAPL to leaning constructive (second closes over their 10-day), AMZN to neutral (a second close over its 50-day), TSLA to cautious (a close under its 50-day), PLTR and SKHY to avoid (171.26 and 137.14 lost). The upgraded cards say the rule fired by points and name the close that reverses it.
  • Firsts, records and lows, checked against the bars with the 10-, 21- and 50-day averages recomputed from them: SPY's −4.4% is the third-largest one-day loss in the loaded history (500 daily bars from Nov 2024) and the largest since Apr 4 2025, the lowest close since Jul 29 and the first close under its 200-day since Apr 2; QQQ, SMH, XLK, MU and SNDK printed the largest one-day losses in their loaded histories, NVDA, AMD and SKHY their second-largest, TSLA its fourth. Lowest closes since: QQQ Apr 21, SMH Apr 13, XLK May 4, NVDA Apr 7, AMD May 5, MU May 7, SNDK Apr 8, MRVL Apr 16, INTC Apr 6, IONQ Apr 22, CRWV Apr 30, HOOD May 27, TSLA Aug 18, PLTR and IGV Aug 3, SPCX Aug 6, ORCL Jul 24, AVGO Aug 21, META Sep 2; SKHY's is the lowest in its loaded history. 52-week lows printed in ORCL, CRWV, IONQ and SKHY. The 200-day was lost by SPY, QQQ, IGV, XLK, AMD (first close under since Mar 6), MU (since May 2025), PLTR (since Aug 3) and TSLA (since Oct 23, with its 50-day since Oct 16). AAPL's 355.38 is the highest print in the loaded history; its close is not.
  • Hourly bars and the daily bar can differ by cents. SPY's last hourly close reads 733.13 against a 733.00 daily close, MU's 658.44 against 656.39, AMD's 402.51 against 404.40; closes and ranges are quoted from the daily bar and intraday paths from the hourly bars.
  • The daily screenshots show price and volume from the layout; every EMA, RSI, MACD and extension figure in a caption is computed from the scan, not read off the image. Every image carries the platform's pre-market quote label this morning; no figure in this report comes from it.
  • Thin histories: SKHY (no EMA200, no weekly badge), SPCX (no daily EMA200, no weekly badge), CRWV (no weekly EMA200). SKHY's and SPCX's EMA50 are the scan's values on their short histories.
  • The scorecard grades the seven Nov 5 calls on Thursday's hourly bars: none of the longs triggered because every open landed under its hold or over its first target; the MSFT and AAPL shorts worked, the NVDA short was a partial and the AMZN short failed. Thirteen off-list cards are graded in the playbook's framing.

Bottom line

  • Every name fell, an average −9.3% on a 2.06× median volume: SPY −4.4% to 733.00, its worst day since April 2025; QQQ −6.5%, SMH −11.2% and XLK −8.0%, their worst in the loaded history.
  • The index closed under its 200-day for the first time since April, 51 cents under it at 1% of range; the running weekly bar sits 19.57 under the 21-week average that held for 30 weeks.
  • Chips and memory led down: SNDK −22.3%, MU −17.5% and AMD −17.3% printed the worst or second-worst days of their histories; NVDA −9.3% closed at its lowest since April.
  • Three charts held their averages: MSFT, AAPL and AMZN are the only names over their 21-, 50- and 200-day, and their cards upgraded on their own rules by points, each naming its reversal close.
  • No Nov 5 long triggered; the MSFT and AAPL shorts paid. Payrolls land at 08:30, today's close sets the weekly bar, and Fear & Greed reads 20, extreme fear, from 35.

Scorecard: the Nov 5 calls against Thursday's bars (0 worked, 0 failed, 7 not triggered; the MSFT and AAPL shorts worked, NVDA partial, AMZN failed)

A gap day in the other direction, and again most day-trade calls were non-events. AMD, TSLA and MU opened under their holds and under the short's first target, so neither side set up; AAPL opened a cent over its first target and AMZN over its own, so neither long was an entry. MSFT opened between its hold and its reclaim and the first hour closed under the 542.30 line, so its short was on from there and printed both targets in the next hour; AAPL's short was on from the 10:30 hour's close under 347.42 and printed both targets by 12:30. NVDA's first hour printed both short targets before it closed, so the entry had nothing left to print and the close 0.65 ATR in favour grades a partial; AMZN's first hour did the same and the day bounced 0.43 ATR against the entry, a failure. Off the calls list, the GOOGL, META and CRWV shorts printed a target after the entry, PLTR and HOOD were washes, and the chip and memory names opened under their short targets with no trade.

Full read: Thursday's session, where it leaves the board, and what today decides

Thursday was the widest down day in the loaded history for most of the board. All 25 names fell, an average −9.3%, on a 2.06× median volume against Wednesday's 1.39×, with every name over its 20-day average. Every name printed its high in the first hour; ten printed the low in the 10:30 hour and bounced, and eleven, the index, the semis wrapper and the chip and memory names, printed the low in the last hour. Fifteen closed in the bottom 15% of their range. SNDK −22.3%, MU −17.5%, AMD −17.3% and MRVL −16.4% were the bottom four; AAPL −1.5%, AMZN −2.2% and GOOGL −2.2% the top three, and the index lost 4.4% to 733.00.

Where it leaves the board. The daily column reads 0 up, 4 mixed and 21 down, from 2 / 3 / 20: MSFT and AAPL came off up to mixed, SPY and TSLA turned down from mixed, AMZN stays mixed. Three names close above their 21-day, their 50-day and their 200-day, MSFT, AAPL and AMZN, from four, five and eleven; SPY, QQQ, IGV, XLK, AMD, MU, PLTR and TSLA lost the 200-day in one bar. Twenty daily charts sit more than two ATR under their mean, from nine, and eleven past three, from two: INTC −4.75, MRVL −4.35, SNDK −4.32, XLK −4.13, NVDA −4.08, SMH −4.06 and MU −4.05 lead. One histogram is positive, AMZN's, and five narrowed.

What today decides. Payrolls at 08:30 print before the open. Whether the index closes the week under its 752.57 weekly EMA21 for the first time in 31 weeks: the running close is 19.57 under it and only today's close counts. Whether the three megacap charts hold their 10-day, MSFT at 530.91, AAPL at 343.19 and AMZN at 253.89, the closes that reverse their upgrades. Whether the chips' last-hour lows hold a first hour: NVDA 181.46, AMD 402.10, MU 650.00, SNDK 803.97, with Nasdaq futures higher on the feed before the open. IONQ opens on gap rules, and Fear & Greed reads 20, extreme fear, from 35.

Day-trading playbook

Friday trades the jobs report into a board that closed on its lows: the three charts over their averages are bought only on a hold of their 10-day neighbourhood (MSFT 533.02–532.68, AAPL 343.19–342.06, AMZN 258.65–255.91), the chips are bought only on a first hour that holds Thursday's last-hour low (NVDA 181.46, AMD 402.10, MU 650.00, SNDK 803.97) and sold only on a loss of it held an hour, IONQ opens on gap rules, and today's close sets the weekly bar.

Session framing

Thursday printed the day's high in the first hour in all 25 names; ten printed the low in the 10:30 hour and bounced, eleven printed it in the last hour, and fifteen closed in the bottom 15% of their range. The shorts that paid were on from a first-hour close under the card's line with the open over it: MSFT, AAPL (from the 10:30 hour), GOOGL, META and CRWV printed a target after the entry. The chip and memory names opened under every short target and had no trade, and no long on the board triggered. The index lost its 200-day and the chip wrapper closed at its lowest since April.

Four questions govern the session. Do the three megacap charts hold their 10-day on the first test, MSFT at 530.91, AAPL at 343.19 and AMZN at 253.89, the closes that reverse their upgrades: an open under MSFT's 527.71, AAPL's 341.79 or AMZN's 253.56 is not bought until the card's reclaim prints on an hourly close. Do the chips' last-hour lows hold a first hour with Nasdaq futures higher on the feed, or does a loss of them held an hour run to the one-ATR targets. Does the index close the week under 752.57 for the first time in 31 weeks. And where does IONQ open against 24.92 and 29.12.

Methodology and data notes

Pipeline, rubric, data caveats and sources

Pipeline: TradingView Desktop (CDP) → dedicated "B List Research" layout → up to 500 bars per timeframe per symbol (W / D / 240 / 60 / 15, regular sessions) → indicators computed locally: EMA 10/21/50/200, RSI-14 (Wilder), MACD 12/26/9, ATR-14 (Wilder), 20-bar relative volume, fractal (2-2) swing pivots, 252-day high/low distances, relative strength vs SPY as return differentials. Trend matrix rubric per cell, ±1 for each of six inputs: close vs EMA21, close vs EMA50, EMA21/EMA50 stack, EMA50 five-bar slope, RSI zone (≥55 = +1, ≤45 = −1, else 0) and MACD histogram sign — score ≥+4 Up, ≤−4 Down, else Chop; cells lacking an EMA21 or EMA50 return "—".

Data caveats. Captured Friday Nov 6 2026 at 07:43 ET, before the open; no errors were reported across the 25 symbols and every symbol ends on Thursday Nov 5's completed session on every frame. No pre-market stub was found and nothing was patched. The prior scan for every day-over-day comparison (change chips, breadth tile, census) is Thursday morning's, which held Wednesday Nov 4's completed session, so every delta on this page is exactly one session, Thursday's. The weekly column is the running Nov 2–6 bar, four sessions old, and its badges are provisional until today's close; SPY's running close sits 19.57 under its 21-week average after 30 completed weeks over it, and that streak is recounted each Saturday. "Thursday" in the cards is Nov 5, "Wednesday" Nov 4, "Tuesday" Nov 3, "Monday" Nov 2 and "Friday" Oct 30; today's session is "today" or "the open". Every time in this report is Eastern standard time; hours are named by the time they open ("the first hour" is 09:30–10:30, "the last hour" 15:30–16:00). The 15m column is Thursday's 15:45 ET bar. The final 15m bars carry the usual closing-auction volume spike and those RVOL figures were not used anywhere in this report; 15-minute readings quoted are RSI, extension and EMA position only. The same applies to 1H and 4H relative volume. All relative-volume figures in this report are daily. Hourly bars and the daily bar can differ by cents at the open and the close (auction prints); closes and ranges are quoted from the daily bar and intraday paths from the hourly bars. Fractal pivot lag. Swing pivots require two bars on each side to confirm, so a level set within the last two bars will not yet appear in the pivot sequence; Monday Nov 2's lows have confirmed as pivots in QQQ, XLK, MSFT, META, AMD, ORCL and IONQ and Tuesday Nov 3's highs in SPCX and AVGO, and no Wednesday or Thursday level is in any list yet. Those sessions' highs and lows are quoted from the bars, not the pivot lists. "Lowest close since", "largest one-day loss in the loaded history", "first close under … since" and "N lower closes" claims were checked against the daily bars with the 10-, 21-, 50- and 200-day averages recomputed from them; every 200-day figure quoted is the scan's, and the recomputed 200-day can differ from it by up to a dollar on 500 bars (SPY 733.87 recomputed against 733.51 in the scan, the close under both). The loaded history is 500 daily bars from Nov 2024, so "worst day in the loaded history" means the largest one-day loss in that window and the 52-week high is the trailing 252 bars. SKHY's and SPCX's daily EMA50 are the scan's values on their short histories. IONQ reported Thursday after the close; its direction is not on the feed and its card opens on gap rules. AMD is two sessions past its print and its card trades Thursday's bar. CRWV reports Tue Nov 10 and NVDA Tue Nov 17. AAPL and PLTR are three sessions past their prints and are read as ordinary bars, as are AMZN, INTC, SNDK, MSFT, GOOGL and META from last week. The midterm result and Thursday's selloff reached this report only through the headline feed, direction only. The daily screenshots inlined in the cards and the market frame show price and volume from the layout; every EMA, RSI, MACD and extension figure quoted in a caption is computed from the scan, not read off the image. Every image carries the platform's pre-market quote label this morning; no figure in this report comes from it. Thin histories: SKHY and SPCX have no weekly badge and no daily EMA200; CRWV has no weekly EMA200.

Scorecard. The Nov 5 edition's seven flagged calls, written on Wednesday's close, are graded against Thursday's hourly and daily bars: the hourly bars decide "held an hour" and the daily close decides the invalidation. An open over the long's first target is not an entry, by a cent in AAPL's case, and an open under the card's hold and under the short's first target sets up neither side (AMD, TSLA, MU, and SNDK, MRVL, INTC, SKHY, SPCX and AVGO off the list). A short is on from the close of the first hour that closes under its line when the open sits over the line (MSFT; GOOGL, META, CRWV, HOOD and PLTR off the list) and from a later hour's close when the line is first closed under then (AAPL's 10:30 hour); a short whose first hour prints every target before it closes has nothing left to print and is graded on the close against the entry (NVDA a partial at 0.65 ATR in favour, AMZN a failure at 0.43 ATR against). A target printed inside the entry hour does not count (NVDA, AMZN, HOOD, PLTR). A trade that prints a target after the entry and closes in its favour is worked (the MSFT and AAPL shorts; GOOGL and META off the list); one that prints a target after the entry and closes back through the entry is a partial (CRWV); one with no target and a close within a fifth of an ATR of the entry is a wash (PLTR, HOOD). A secondary trade on the same card is graded in the note and not in the tally. Stance changes follow each card's own stated rule: MSFT and AAPL printed a second close over their 10-day (leaning constructive), AMZN a second close over its 50-day (neutral), TSLA a close under its 50-day (cautious), PLTR a close under 171.26 and SKHY a close under 137.14 (avoid). The three upgrades fired by points on the day the index fell 4.4%; the rule is applied as written and each card names the close that reverses it.
